raw_issue.description: Opening a browser-owned conversation in the Agent Coord macOS app fails because BrowserSessions.read calls thread/resume for any locally unloaded, open thread. Each UI backend has its own Codex app-server and in-memory loaded set, despite sharing the Agent Coord database. Viewing therefore attempts to acquire a second Codex writer. Investigation reproduced HTTP 400 on both a running thread (01a1174d-dd82-7421-9a03-9671251c8671) and an idle thread (01a1174a-713b-7e41-90af-f847c01e71fb). The browser backend was PID 51770 on port 8765, its writer was Codex PID 54757, and the macOS backend was PID 637 on port 63473. lsof and a nonblocking flock check confirmed the browser holds the running thread writer lock. An independent app-server thread/read with includeTurns=true succeeded for that same thread without thread/started. Installed browser and native snapshots both contain resume-on-open behavior. Separate viewing from writer acquisition and design owner routing or explicit safe transfer for sending; a controlled shared conversation backend is an alternative. Do not stop shared active servers or delete legitimate writer lock files to work around this. Browser tab closure does not release server ownership. No implementation was performed during investigation.
raw_issue.design:
Proposal for seamless browser/native sharing; not implemented or approved.

Use one shared Agent Coord conversation service per canonical database. It owns BrowserSessions, Codex writer connections, queues, pending approvals/questions, and event streaming. Browser and macOS launchers discover and attach to this verified service instead of creating independent writers.

Use atomic startup locking plus service identity and protocol/version validation. Preserve the native app's rule against attaching to arbitrary servers on remembered ports; its current private adapter can proxy to a verified shared conversation service or become a thin launcher/client.

Closing or quitting a frontend detaches that client. Shared process lifetime belongs to the service, with an explicit shutdown or safe idle retirement; active turns and input requests must survive loss of one frontend.

Separate read-only viewing (thread/read) from writer attachment (thread/resume). Conversations owned by independent terminal processes still require clear owner/transfer behavior; do not automatically take over active owners.

Migration must let existing turns/input requests finish and release verified old owners before the new service resumes persisted conversations. Do not kill active servers to migrate.

issue.title: Reuse loaded conversation when reopening from overview
issue.description: Investigation of Ribbon Field overview → session → overview → same session found repeated full-history work in the installed app. web/app.js goHome clears state.detail; select clears it again and replaces the retained timeline with Opening session before awaiting two serial GETs (threads then sessions). refreshDetail then rebuilds every transcript item, including collapsed tool-output bodies. BrowserSessions.read retains the loaded provider session but always calls _read_thread; _remember_thread deep-copies the transcript and calls _save_history on every successful read, which serializes and rewrites browser_history even when unchanged. Live warm reads of stoic product engineering returned 7,226,258 bytes and 1,275 items and took 0.58–0.63 seconds for sessions GET alone. Small loaded conversations took 20–30 ms. An isolated profile with the real large transcript and a fake provider attributed 170 ms of a 209 ms read to _remember_thread, including 108 ms in _save_history; these profiled times are diagnostic, not a frontend latency measurement. Recommendation: restore cached per-thread conversation display immediately on return, refresh authoritative history/state in the background, and avoid full-history persistence when content is unchanged. Preserve streamed updates, approval safety, seen/completion markers, and scroll/drafts. No production code changed during investigation.
issue.acceptance_criteria: Reopening an already viewed session displays retained history without waiting for full transcript GETs; cached state reconciles with live events and background refresh; unchanged backend reads do not rewrite full history; regression validation covers overview return, updates while hidden, and large transcripts.
